bull_bear.body:
- Jayhawk acquisition (~$150Mn total consideration) funded through a combination of internal accruals, debt and quasi equity.
- Bliss GVS Pharma acquisition structured via a non-controlling non-voting equity instrument (~₹1,300 Cr) plus a term loan (~₹300 Cr), avoiding a straightforward equity stake purchase.
- Growth phase (2023-24) financed through capital markets: ₹5,000 Mn QIP and ₹5,500 Mn Preferential Issue.

business.body:
- Positions as a fast-growing Specialty Chemical Manufacturer focused on Custom Synthesis, with longstanding relationships with leading MNCs, deep expertise across complex chemistries, and platforms spanning Agro, Personal Care, Pharma and Performance Materials.
- 4-decade track record, backward integrated for reliable supply chain to customers, 200+ clients including 55+ MNCs.
- World's first company to commercialize ETFA (Ethyl Trifluoroacetate) using flow chemistry, underscoring differentiated capability in complex fluorination.
- Integrated platform: Tanfac (HF/KF critical raw-material production) feeds Anupam Rasayan's custom synthesis and Jayhawk's advanced intermediates, together spanning polymers, electronic chemicals, API intermediates and crop-protection actives for high-value end markets.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Completed acquisition of Jayhawk Fine Chemicals Corporation (Kansas, US; founded 1941) - manufactures performance materials (~65%) and life/crop science molecules (~35%); FY revenue ~$76Mn, EBITDA ~$15Mn (~19% margin), ~140 employees.
- [Acquisition] Definitive agreement to acquire Bliss GVS Pharma - first EU-GMP certified suppositories manufacturer in India, flagship WHO-endorsed anti-malarial brand Lonart, 6 manufacturing facilities across Palghar/Vevoor/Ambernath (Maharashtra), 150+ brands, 50+ therapeutic segments, 1,000+ employees; recent USFDA approval for the Palghar suppository unit.
- [Corporate structure] Group platforms as of FY26: Tanfac Industries (fluorochemicals subsidiary, ₹711 Cr revenue, 1.35L MT capacity), Bliss GVS Pharma (proposed group holding 43.3-48.2%+open offer, ₹927 Cr revenue, 4,822 Mn units capacity), Jayhawk (wholly-owned subsidiary, ₹722 Cr* revenue, 36,000 MT capacity).
- [Leadership] Experienced management: MD Mr. Anand S Desai (30+ yrs, with company since 1992), Vice-Chairperson Mrs. Mona A Desai (20+ yrs), CEO Mr. Gopal Agrawal (ex-MD & Head-IB at Edelweiss), WTD & R&D Head Dr. Anuj Thakar (~18 yrs), COO Mr. Ravi Desai (~14 yrs), CFO Mr. Amit Khurana (~10 yrs), Technical Head Dr. Nileshkumar Naik (since incorporation).
business.title: Notable from the deck

outlook.body: revenue growth, margin, order inflow, capex/commissioning
outlook.title: Guidance

open.item: Quarterly interest expense expected around Rs.26-27 crore or a little less as debt reduces
Consol gross debt ~Rs.1,500 crore (net ~Rs.1,100 cr), over two-thirds working capital loan; adding ~Rs.300 cr for Bliss to ~Rs.1,400-1,500 cr net vs Rs.650-800 cr EBITDA
Signed definitive agreement to acquire 43.3%-48.2% equity in Bliss GVS Pharma plus open offer up to 26%; timeline 2-3 months subject to SEBI/open offer
Elementium (MIT-backed) electrolyte LOI: commercialization expected 2026 from existing capacity; 10x higher volumes post-2026 will need added capacity
FY26 operating cash flow Rs.334 crore on improved working capital; further improvement expected in FY27
Consolidated working capital ~215-220 days pro forma (240-250 days ex-Jayhawk); trajectory to keep improving in FY27
Expect significant increase in revenue in FY27 (volume and value) from the key agro AI molecule; no further capex required currently

Signed long-term master purchase agreement with a Japanese fluorochemicals conglomerate for 5-6 polymer molecules (semiconductors, data centers, electronics); several to commercialize this year, ramp from next year
Fluorination chemistry to be 20%-25% of revenue this year (FY25) and 30%-35% by 2027
Goal of being energy net zero by 2027
Peak revenue from LOI pipeline (previously FY27) now expected largely by FY28, with commercialization in FY26-27
Separate ~Rs.250 crore Halol CDMO capex (for a large MNC pharma customer) with expected 4x-5x asset turnover, executed independently
Target 20% to 25% or 30% revenue CAGR (standalone) over the next 3 to 5 years
Bliss synergies and cross-leverage expected to start giving results in 6-12 months, larger benefits in 18 months
Vision to build dedicated pharma platform via Bliss GVS as primary vehicle for future pharma CDMO/CMO; all new pharma products/BD to gradually integrate into it
Standalone tax rate expected ~25% going forward
Order book ~Rs.14,000 crore; on 6-7 year average ~Rs.1,700-1,800 crore incremental annual revenue can come from this pipeline (agro + polymer)
Standalone gross block (~Rs.2,500-2,600 cr) can deliver peak revenue of ~Rs.3,500 crore
Standalone maintenance capex expected ~Rs.50-75 crore per year over next 2-3 years
Bliss operating at ~30% capacity utilization (~Rs.1,000 cr top line); to be enhanced to 60%-70% in near to medium term with proportionate revenue

verdicts.item: Targeting 180 to 200 days net working capital over next 18-24 months
verdicts.note: '215 to 220-odd days... on a pro forma basis'; 'excluding Jayhawk... 240 to 250 days' - approaching 180-200 days target [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Performance materials (polymer) to be ~15%-20% of revenue this year, reaching 20%-25% in next 2-3 years
verdicts.note: 'Performance Materials contributed 18% of our revenue' - within the 15-20%-this-year guidance

verdicts.item: US geography to contribute over 15% of sales over next 2-3 years (high teens by end of next year / 12-18 months) on new contract and LOI
verdicts.note: 'successfully completed the acquisition of Jayhawk... strategic manufacturing footprint in the U.S.' - US contribution materially advanced, no % stated

verdicts.item: No further capex planned; future free cash flow to convert into debt reduction
verdicts.note: 'not envisaging any major capex in near future'; strong operating cash flow INR334 cr, but acquisitions funded via debt - self-funding held for organic, acquisitions add debt

verdicts.item: Stronger Agrochem numbers expected from Q4 FY25 and into FY26 as demand strengthens especially from Europe
verdicts.note: 'agro is kind of performing well. The volumes are kind of coming back'; standalone FY26 growth 60-70% aided by agro recovery

verdicts.item: Expect to return to historical growth rate of 25% to 30%-plus from FY26 onwards (standalone)
verdicts.note: 'over 60% to 70% growth rate in our annual revenues' - well above 25-30%+ target

verdicts.item: FY26 EBITDA margins expected similar to historical 26% to 28% range
verdicts.note: '23% for FY26' - below the guided 26-28% FY26 range [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: FY26 revenue phasing expected ~40%-45% in H1 and ~55%-60% in H2 due to industry cyclicity
verdicts.note: H1 revenue INR1,217 cr of FY26 INR2,384 cr = ~51% - front-loaded vs the guided 40-45% H1 / 55-60% H2 phasing

verdicts.item: Rs.670 crore capex nearly complete; two facilities commercialized, one new manufacturing facility ready for commercialization in the upcoming quarter
verdicts.note: 'all our plants are commercialized' - the plant that was in trial runs is commercialized

verdicts.item: Order book ~Rs.14,646 crore spread over 4-10 years; Rs.3,100 crore commercialized (over 20% of FY25 revenue); majority of balance to commercialize in FY26
verdicts.note: 'order book itself is around about INR14,000 crores' - order book maintained, balance commercializing [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Current gross block plus new plant can deliver Rs.3,000-3,500 crore revenue (ex-battery capex)
verdicts.note: 'we should be looking at about INR3,500 crores kind of a number from this block' - reaffirmed (forward potential) [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: FY26 expected mix: Pharma 20%-25%, Performance chemicals 25%+, Personal care ~8%-10%, balance agro
verdicts.note: 'Pharma... 20%... Performance Materials... 18%... Personal Care 7%' - pharma at low end of 20-25%; performance 18% below 25%+; PC 7% below 8-10%

wtt.tone_latest: Confident and expansive: management highlighted the landmark FY26 and framed the Tanfac/Jayhawk/Bliss platform strategy, but repeatedly invoked 'safe harbour' and declined specifics on Bliss pending deal consummation; acknowledged the FY24-25 lost years being recouped.
